Query: complete legal compliance checklist for an Indian AI startup with employees, user data, proprietary model code, GST billing and outside investors
Valid as of: 2026-10-15

SUMMARY
- Corporate Governance: Corporate governance for startups requires compliance with share capital structures, board appointments, and the procedural conduct of general meetings.
- Corporate Governance: Startups must ensure statutory financial disclosures, maintain minutes of proceedings, and authorize corporate representatives as mandated.
- Corporate Governance (not addressed by retrieved provisions): The specific internal governance regarding proprietary model code protection is not covered by these corporate governance provisions.
- Data Protection: Artificial intelligence startups must act as Data Fiduciaries, ensuring lawful processing, obtaining informed consent, implementing security safeguards, and managing data breaches.
- Data Protection: Compliance includes providing transparent notices, establishing grievance redressal mechanisms, and ensuring child safety in digital data processing.
- Data Protection: some of these obligations are not yet in force on 2026-10-15; each step below shows the date it applies from.
- Data Protection (not addressed by retrieved provisions): The provisions do not provide specific technical guidelines for AI model training or data curation beyond the general requirements of the Data Protection Act.
- Intellectual Property: Computer programs are protected as 'literary works' under copyright law, with employers typically owning rights to works created by employees under contract.
- Intellectual Property: Copyright can be assigned through written agreements, and specific restrictions apply to patenting inventions abroad.
- Intellectual Property (not addressed by retrieved provisions): The provisions do not address the specific patentability of 'models' beyond noting that computer programs per se are not patentable inventions, nor do they provide specific protection mechanisms for trade secrets.
- Taxation & GST: Registered persons must issue compliant tax invoices for taxable supplies or bills of supply for exempted supplies.
- Taxation & GST: Tax liability arises based on the time of supply, determined by the earlier of invoice issuance or payment receipt.
- Taxation & GST (not addressed by retrieved provisions): The provisions do not specify unique billing requirements based on company size (e.g., small startup vs large enterprise) or employee type.
- Employment & Workplace: Employers must comply with statutory requirements for anti-sexual harassment committees, gratuity, provident funds, maternity benefits, and retrenchment protocols.
- Employment & Workplace: Compliance involves procedural duties such as training, internal investigations, contribution payments, and documentation.
- Employment & Workplace (not addressed by retrieved provisions): The provided provisions do not address general employment contract requirements, minimum wage laws, or health and safety standards outside the context of sexual harassment or accident-related medical aid.

ACTION CHECKLIST
**Corporate Governance**
Step 1: Classify share capital as either equity (with or without differential rights) or preference share capital, the latter carrying preferential rights to dividends and repayment of capital during winding up. — [ca_2013_sec_43] (applies to: both)
Step 2: Vary rights attached to a class of shares only with the written consent of three-fourths of the class holders or a special resolution at a separate meeting; dissenters holding at least 10% may apply to the Tribunal for cancellation. — [ca_2013_sec_48] (applies to: both) [NOTE: only partly supported by the cited text]
Step 3: Ensure directors possess a Director Identification Number and provide written consent to the Registrar within 30 days of appointment; first directors are subscribers to the memorandum if the articles are silent. — [ca_2013_sec_152] (applies to: both) [NOTE: only partly supported by the cited text]
Step 4: Issue securities via rights issue, bonus issue, or private placement (for private companies) or via public offer/prospectus/private placement (for public companies). — [ca_2013_sec_23] (applies to: both)
Step 5: Have the Board approve financial statements and ensure they are signed by the chairperson, CEO, CFO, and company secretary; attach the Board's Report including the Directors' Responsibility Statement and disclosure of related party contracts. — [ca_2013_sec_134] (applies to: both)
Step 6: Hold an annual general meeting (AGM) during business hours on a non-National Holiday; hold the first AGM within nine months of the first financial year end, and subsequent AGMs within six months of each financial year end. — [ca_2013_sec_96] (applies to: both)
Step 7: Prepare and sign minutes of all board and general meetings within 30 days of the conclusion of the meeting, keep them in consecutive numbered pages, and observe secretarial standards. — [ca_2013_sec_118] (applies to: both) [NOTE: only partly supported by the cited text]
Step 8: Circulate copies of audited financial statements, auditor's reports, and annexures to every member not less than 21 days before the general meeting. — [ca_2013_sec_136] (applies to: both) [NOTE: only partly supported by the cited text]
Step 9: Annex a statement to the notice of general meetings detailing material facts and the interest of directors, managers, and other key managerial personnel regarding special business items. — [ca_2013_sec_102] (applies to: both) [NOTE: only partly supported by the cited text]
Step 10: Authorize a representative via a Board resolution for a body corporate (such as an outside investor) to act and vote on its behalf at company meetings. — [ca_2013_sec_113] (applies to: both)

**Data Protection**
Step 11: The Data Fiduciary must determine the purpose and means of processing personal data and ensure compliance with the Act, regardless of any contrary agreement. — [dpdp_act_2023_sec_2] (applies to: both) [NOTE: only partly supported by the cited text]
Step 12: Process personal data only for a lawful purpose, defined as any purpose not expressly forbidden by law, based on consent or legitimate uses. — [dpdp_act_2023_sec_4] (applies to: both) [NOTE: Not yet in force on 2026-10-15; applies from 2027-05-13.]
Step 13: Provide a notice to the Data Principal before or at the time of seeking consent, detailing the data collected, the purpose of processing, and how to exercise rights or complain to the Board. — [dpdp_act_2023_sec_5] (applies to: both) [NOTE: Not yet in force on 2026-10-15; applies from 2027-05-13.]
Step 14: Ensure consent is free, specific, informed, unconditional, and unambiguous; allow for withdrawal of consent with comparable ease to the original grant, and cease processing upon withdrawal. — [dpdp_act_2023_sec_6] (applies to: both) [NOTE: Not yet in force on 2026-10-15; applies from 2027-05-13.]
Step 15: Protect personal data using reasonable security safeguards, maintain effective grievance redressal, and, unless legally required otherwise, erase data when consent is withdrawn or the purpose is served. — [dpdp_act_2023_sec_8] (applies to: both) [NOTE: Not yet in force on 2026-10-15; applies from 2027-05-13.]
Step 16: Obtain verifiable parental consent before processing children's data and avoid tracking, behavioural monitoring, or targeted advertising directed at children. — [dpdp_act_2023_sec_9] (applies to: both) [NOTE: Not yet in force on 2026-10-15; applies from 2027-05-13.]
Step 17: Note that certain startup entities may be exempted by the Central Government from specific notice and processing obligations under the Act. — [dpdp_act_2023_sec_17] (applies to: both) [NOTE: Not yet in force on 2026-10-15; applies from 2027-05-13.]
Step 18: Comply with the specific requirements for notice presentation, including using clear language, itemizing data categories, and providing communication links for consent withdrawal and complaints. — [dpdp_rules_2025_sec_3] (applies to: both) [NOTE: Not yet in force on 2026-10-15; applies from 2027-05-13.]
Step 19: Intimate the Board and affected Data Principals regarding any personal data breach with specific details on the nature of the breach, mitigation measures, and contact information. — [dpdp_rules_2025_sec_7] (applies to: both) [NOTE: only partly supported by the cited text] [NOTE: Not yet in force on 2026-10-15; applies from 2027-05-13.]
Step 20: Publish and maintain business contact information for a person or Data Protection Officer designated to address Data Principal inquiries regarding data processing. — [dpdp_rules_2025_sec_9] (applies to: both) [NOTE: Not yet in force on 2026-10-15; applies from 2027-05-13.]
Step 21: Adhere to penalties ranging from ten thousand to two hundred and fifty crore rupees for breaches of obligations related to security, notice, child protection, and other provisions. — [dpdp_act_2023_sch_1] (applies to: both) [NOTE: only partly supported by the cited text] [NOTE: Not yet in force on 2026-10-15; applies from 2027-05-13.]

**Intellectual Property**
Step 22: Classify your proprietary computer programs as 'literary works' to establish copyright protection eligibility. — [copyright_act_1957_sec_2]
Step 23: Exercise your exclusive rights as a copyright owner, which includes the right to reproduce, adapt, and commercially rent your computer programs. — [copyright_act_1957_sec_14]
Step 24: Ensure that your startup (as the employer) is the first owner of copyright for code created by employees in the course of their employment, unless a contract states otherwise. — [copyright_act_1957_sec_17] (applies to: private)
Step 25: Ensure code is original and published in India (or authored by an Indian citizen if published abroad) for copyright to subsist. — [copyright_act_1957_sec_13]
Step 26: Assign copyright of your code in whole or in part, noting that assignments for future works only take effect once the work exists, and cannot apply to media not in commercial use at the time of assignment. — [copyright_act_1957_sec_18]
Step 27: Execute all copyright assignments in writing signed by the assignor, explicitly stating the rights, duration, and territory (defaults apply if these are omitted: 5 years duration and India-wide territory). — [copyright_act_1957_sec_19]

**Taxation & GST**
Step 28: A registered person must issue a tax invoice before or at the time of removal/delivery for goods, and within a prescribed period for services. For exempted supplies or those under section 10, a bill of supply must be issued instead, unless the value is less than two hundred rupees. — [cgst_act_2017_sec_31] (applies to: both)
Step 29: When issuing a bill of supply, the supplier must include specific details such as the supplier's name, address, and GSTIN, a unique serial number, date of issue, recipient details, HSN code, description of supply, value (after discount/abatement), and signature/digital signature. — [cgst_rules_2017_rule_49] (applies to: both)
Step 30: The time of supply for goods is the earlier of the date of invoice issuance (or the last date required to issue it) or the date of payment receipt. For supplies under reverse charge, it is the earliest of the date of receipt of goods or the date of payment. — [cgst_act_2017_sec_12] (applies to: both) [NOTE: only partly supported by the cited text]
Step 31: The time of supply for services is the earlier of the invoice issue date (if issued within the prescribed period) or payment receipt date; otherwise, it is the date of provision of service. — [cgst_act_2017_sec_13] (applies to: both)

**Employment & Workplace**
Step 32: Prohibit sexual harassment at the workplace and address specific conduct that constitutes harassment. — [posh_2013_sec_3] (applies to: both)
Step 33: Provide a safe working environment, display penal consequences, conduct awareness workshops, and treat sexual harassment as misconduct under service rules. — [posh_2013_sec_19] (applies to: both) [NOTE: only partly supported by the cited text]
Step 34: Constitute an Internal Complaints Committee via written order at every office/administrative unit with prescribed composition, and ensure members meet tenure and qualification requirements. — [posh_2013_sec_4] (applies to: both)
Step 35: Pay gratuity to an employee upon termination after five years of continuous service (waived for death, disablement, or fixed-term contract expiration) at a rate of 15 days' wages per year of service. — [css_2020_sec_53] (applies to: both) [NOTE: only partly supported by the cited text]
Step 36: Allow pregnant employees to be absent upon written notice and pay maternity benefits in advance or within 48 hours of delivery proof, as applicable. — [css_2020_sec_62] (applies to: both) [NOTE: only partly supported by the cited text]
Step 37: Provide one month's notice (or pay in lieu), pay retrenchment compensation of 15 days' average pay per year of service, and notify the appropriate government before retrenching workmen with at least one year of service. — [ida_1947_sec_25F] (applies to: both)
Step 38: Refrain from engaging in unfair labour practices, including victimisation, illegal discharges, favouritism, or interfering with the right to unionise. — [ida_1947_sch_Fifth] (applies to: both)
Step 39: Pay the employer's contribution of 10% (or 12% if notified) of an employee's basic wages, dearness allowance, and retaining allowance to the Provident Fund. — [epf_1952_sec_6] (applies to: both) [NOTE: only partly supported by the cited text]
Step 40: Pay gratuity for termination after five years of service, adhering to the maximum limit of 3.5 lakh rupees, and withhold or forfeit gratuity only in cases of wilful damage or specified misconduct. — [poga_1972_sec_4] (applies to: both) [NOTE: only partly supported by the cited text]
